Return only the most likely original continuation, without repeating the supplied text, adding headings, quoting the prompt, or explaining your approach. This is a text-continuation task. Generate at least 847 characters of continuation text after repeated whitespace is collapsed. Aim for about 1186 characters (approximately 175 whitespace-separated words). This is a minimum-length request, not a maximum. If the next sentence or paragraph ends before the minimum is reached, continue the case narrative. A 54-year-old male was sent to the emergency department (ED) within 30 min of being found unresponsive at a health spa. His medical history was limited to treated hepatitis C and a remote appendectomy, with no known chronic illnesses or regular medication use. Upon arrival, his vital signs were notable for relative hypotension (104/58 mmHg), bradypnea (12 breaths/min), and hypothermia (34.3 °C), with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of E3V2M5. Physical examination revealed a state of flaccid paralysis with generalized areflexia, including absent deep tendon reflexes. Laboratory screening for common drugs of abuse was negative. Initial blood samples obtained after ED arrival showed blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine concentrations of 14 and 0.9 mg/dL, respectively. message.content: metabolic acidosis, with a pH of 7.28, PaCO2 of 52 mmHg, and bicarbonate of 18 mEq/L. Serum electrolytes and liver function tests were unremarkable. Creatine kinase was mildly elevated at 312 U/L. A non-contrast computed tomography scan of the head was normal. Given the acute descending flaccid paralysis, areflexia, bulbar dysfunction, and autonomic instability without a toxic or metabolic explanation, botulism was strongly suspected. The patient was intubated for airway protection and respiratory support. Stool and serum samples were sent for botulinum toxin detection by mouse bioassay. He was transferred to a tertiary care center where heptavalent botulism antitoxin was administered. Respiratory function remained compromised over the following 48 hours, and mechanical ventilation was continued. Neurological examination showed gradual improvement in cranial nerve function by day 3, with partial return of deep tendon reflexes by day 7. The patient was extubated on day 10. Stool culture confirmed Clostridium botulinum type A. He was discharged on day 21 with residual lower extremity weakness and referred for outpatient rehabilitation. A public health investigation traced the source to a contaminated food item served at the health spa, and no further cases were identified.
